### 📓 Docs Drift Check
⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files. Nothing else in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **1** changed package(s)).

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8eef9a8db402b6d46b15cc2375f8acddbb0d7b7e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

2. 前提实测 — PR #26757 merged; the examples are real (`examples/app-crm/src/translations/crm.translation.ts:99`, `examples/app-showcase/src/system/translations/index.ts:1362`); case 6's cut `--no-objects-only` pin stays pinned by case 5 (`must_contain` L50), so no fact left the file.
3. 门禁 check-runs — dev ran the 108 derived commands on the head (87 + 21 from the lint path), all exit 0 (`--ran` 108, 0 NOT-MEASURED); `@objectstack/lint` typecheck and 7430/7430 tests green; build closure VERDICT 0. CI on the head is read again before landing.

The seat patched the PR body (L163 now in this PR; the "not filed" note removed). Payment of the eval row follows 「A:先削重复,余额按实测提高」: 77 B trimmed first, then raised by the measured remainder.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `73e5a8f1d60b4332b2da22a580cbffaff3f6aeeb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md + skills/objectstack-i18n/evals/bundles-locales-coverage.json, scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs, content/docs/ui/translations.mdx, packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts, .changeset/26759-i18n-skill-inline-title-report-blocks.md, packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/report.zod.ts, examples/app-crm/src/translations/crm.translation.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/system/translations/index.ts

Director seat (summon #52, ledger objectstack#12708), summoned by the `domain:skills#1` seat. Read-only at the head above: the diff, card #26759 (filing gate ①, the `Skills-docs:` follow-up owed by #26757), its thread (claim 6449271046, amendment 6449881440, both dev reports), the seat's ACCEPT 6450504495, the eval file as stored at this head and on `origin/main` `0ea90c7a`, the spec docblocks and the two shipped bundles on `main`, the head's check runs. `skills/**` is a governed-register row and publishes (the `@objectstack/skills` bundle) ⇒ the rules face, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`; Tier H, lands on a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` approval, not on this record. Served at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. The seat records; it does not approve, ready, queue or merge.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Both taught keys are the spec's, with the spec's own rule.** `FieldTranslationSchema.inlineTitle` (`translation.zod.ts:134–147` on `main`): the heading of the inline child grid drawn on the PARENT's form, addressed on the child (`objects.<child>.fields.<field>.inlineTitle`), overlaid by `translateObject`, "No fallback to the child object's translated plural label: an authored `inlineTitle` with no entry here keeps its authored text". The skill row and the docs row say exactly that. `reports.<name>.blocks.<block_name>.{label,description}` (`translation.zod.ts:1199`, a `strictObject` keyed "by the block's `name` (`JoinedReportBlockSchema.name`, required)"; `report.zod.ts:280`). The skill sentence, the docs row and the lint header comment all spell it that way.
- **The example rows are the shipped bundles', byte for byte.** `crm.translation.ts:97–99`: `crm_opportunity_line_item: { fields: { opportunity: { inlineTitle: '产品明细' } } }`, under the comment "the field lives on the line item, so the key is the line item's". `app-showcase … translations/index.ts:1361–1363`: `showcase_task_overview … blocks: { open_block: { label: '未完成任务' } … }`. The fragment fence invents nothing; the skill's own todo-mirroring bundle has neither source, so a fence is the right home (dev open question A — agreed).
- **Case 8 grades its own ideal answer right.** Reading the stored head file: every `must_contain` (`inlineTitle`, `crm_opportunity_line_item`, `blocks`, `open_block`) present; neither `must_not_contain` (`fields.opportunity_line_item`, the key on the parent; `components.open_block`, a page-component spelling) present. The refused spellings are the two mistakes an author would actually make.
- **The cut is a duplicate, as the seat read.** Case 6 loses its `os i18n extract --no-objects-only` sentence and the `--no-objects-only` assertion; case 5 on `main` and at the head still pins the flag in `must_contain`. 77 bytes (56 from `expected_output`, 21 from the assertion list), matching the row comment.
- **Ratchet arithmetic at the head.** Eval file stored 5802 → 6567 bytes (+765 = the new case − 77); `ceil(5802/4) = 1451`, `ceil(6567/4) = 1642`, pinned at the measurement, headroom 0, the tap quoted verbatim. `SKILL.md` 21866 − 20 (stamp) = 21846 ⇒ 5462 of 6333, row unmoved. The head's own ratchet row reads `1642`.
- **The lint edit is a comment.** `validate-translation-references.ts:163–165` header only; the validator reads the Zod shape, which already accepts `blocks`. No behaviour, no export.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/skills` takes a `patch` changeset, both declaration lines present at line start and equal to the PR body's. Skill text, an eval and a docs page; `patch` is right. The lint comment edit publishes nothing new.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Governed path (`skills/**`, Tier H): no review yet; draft. This seat's account is not a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` member; this record is not an approval and does not lift Tier H.
- **Should-fix, in this PR's own hunk (same class as #26515):** case 6 — the case this PR edits — still spells its own `must_not_contain` string inside its ideal answer: `expected_output` says "never `permissionSets`" while `must_not_contain` lists `permissionSets`, so the ideal answer is graded wrong. Pre-existing on `main`, but the PR has the case open and the dev's "no `must_contain` string sits in a `must_not_contain`" check does not cover `expected_output` against `must_not_contain`. A same-byte rewording (for example "not the camel-case alias") keeps the file at its 1642 pin; a longer one is paid under the same ruling. Fix here rather than carry it to a third card.
- Check runs on `73e5a8f1` at this record: 42 `success`, 9 expected skips, nothing in progress, nothing red — including `Lint · repo & tooling gates` (the token ratchet), `Check Changeset`, both `Lint · docs & code guards` and the `@objectstack/lint` typecheck/test shards.
- `origin/main` has not moved on any of the six files since the branch's base; no merge-in owed.
- No gate runs the eval; the green proves parse, ratchet, changeset and the doc gates, not that an agent passes case 8 (named, as on #26774 and #26810).
- Note, not a finding: the spec docblock says the inline grid is drawn by "a `master_detail` / `lookup` field with `inlineEdit`"; the skill says `master_detail`. `field.form.ts:294` shows the key only when `type == 'master_detail'` and `field.zod.ts:1675` describes it as the master-detail grid title, so the skill follows the authoring surface. Fine as written.
- Dev deviations: the examples in a fragment fence (judged above); the docs page rides this Tier H PR (the card allowed either; nothing on it is blocked by waiting); the seat patched the body after the round-2 amendment so the L163 bullet now matches the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

- `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md` against the spec: the `inlineTitle` row teaches the one non-obvious fact (the key is the child's, and silence keeps authored text) in the row where an author picks field sub-keys, and the report sentence puts `blocks.{block_name}` beside the `label` + `description` it extends, keyed the way `pages.{page}.components.{id}` already taught. Case 8's prompt gives real object, field, report and block names from shipped bundles, so a candidate cannot pass by paraphrase, and its refusals are the two plausible wrong addresses. The docs twin carries the same two rows with the same rule. Holds; nothing to break.
